Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, answered this question, saying: ﴿About the great news, about which they are in disagreement﴾ [an-Naba' 1–3]. People have differed about this news that the Prophet (ﷺ) brought: some of them believed and affirmed it, and some of them disbelieved and denied it. Allah made clear that those who denied will surely come to know, they will surely come to know what they denied with certain knowledge, and that will be when they see it on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿On the Day when its interpretation comes, those who had forgotten it before will say, "The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth"﴾ [al-A'raf 53]. They are of differing pairs according to what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, willed and wisdom required, so that people may take a lesson from Allah's power, and that He is able to make this human race, which was created from one substance and one father, into these diverse and varied kinds.

That is why you find that when a man becomes tired and then sleeps, he rests and his energy is renewed. This is from the blessing, and at the same time it is one of the signs of Allah, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day, and your seeking of His bounty﴾ [ar-Rum 23].

Allah made clear that those who denied will surely come to know, they will surely come to know what they denied with certain knowledge, and that will be when they see it on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿On the Day when its interpretation comes, those who had forgotten it before will say, "The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth"﴾ [al-A'raf 53]. The knowledge with which Allah threatens them is the certain knowledge that they will witness in accordance with what they were told. Then Allah, the Exalted, explained His blessings upon His servants, in order to establish these blessings so that they become obligated to thank Him for them, and He said: ﴿Have We not made the earth a resting place (6), and the mountains as pegs (7), and created you in pairs (8), and made your sleep a means of rest (9)﴾ [an-Naba' 6–9], and so on to the end.

May the blessings and peace of Allah be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 78, verse 17–20:

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, the Day of Judgment is an appointed time﴾ [An-Naba' 17]. It is the Day of Resurrection, and it is called the Day of Separation (Yawm al-Fasl) because Allah separates on it among His servants concerning what they disputed among themselves and what they used to differ over. He separates between the people of truth and the people of falsehood, the people of disbelief and the people of faith, the people of transgression and the people of moderation. He also separates on it between the people of Paradise and the people of Hellfire: a group in Paradise and a group in the Blaze.

And ﴿was an appointed time﴾ means it is fixed for a specified term, as He said: ﴿And We do not delay it except for a limited term﴾ [Hud 104]. Consider a thing that has a specified term while you see how the term passes swiftly, day after day, until a person reaches the last stage. Likewise, the whole world proceeds day after day until it reaches its last stage. For this reason He said: ﴿And We do not delay it except for a limited term﴾, and everything that is limited will come to an end.

﴿On the Day the Horn is blown, and you will come forth in multitudes﴾ [An-Naba' 18]. The one who blows into it is Israfil, who is appointed over it. He blows it twice: the first, by which people are terrified and then fall unconscious and die; and the second, by which they are resurrected from their graves, and their souls return to them. For this reason He said here: ﴿On the Day the Horn is blown, and you will come forth in multitudes﴾. In the verse, as is evident, there is brevity through omission, meaning: then you will be revived and come forth in multitudes, group after group, or one group following another. These multitudes, and Allah knows best, are according to the nations; each nation is called to its book to be held accountable for it. So people come forth in multitudes in this tremendous station, in which the earth is leveled and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, leaves it as a level plain in which you see no crookedness or elevation.

On that Day Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And the heaven will be opened and will become gates﴾ [An-Naba' 19]. It will be split and opened so that it becomes gates that people can see, after it was previously a protected ceiling. On that Day it will become open gates. In this is evidence of the perfection of Allah's power, Mighty and Majestic, that these seven strong heavens will be made by Allah, Exalted, on the Day of Resurrection as though they had never been, becoming gates. ﴿On the Day the heaven will be like molten brass, and the mountains will be like wool, and no intimate friend will ask about his intimate friend, they will be shown to one another﴾ [Al-Ma'arij 8–11].

﴿And the mountains will be set in motion and will become a mirage﴾ [An-Naba' 20]. That is, the great, solid mountains will be crushed and become like sand, and then they will become like a mirage, moving: ﴿And the mountains will be set in motion and will become a mirage﴾.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Hell has been lying in wait﴾ [An-Naba' 21].

We will leave that for next week, Allah willing, the Exalted.

We complete what we have been going through of the tafsir. We have already spoken on His saying, may He be exalted, in Surah An-Naba about the tyrants (al-Taghun), that Hell was their destination (ma'ab), and that they would remain in it for ages (ahqab): ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness or any drink (24) except boiling water and dark, murderous cold (ghassaq)﴾ [An-Naba 24, 25]. We spoke on His saying: ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness or any drink﴾, and we said: God, glorified and exalted, negated from them the coolness by which the outer surfaces of their bodies are cooled, and the drink by which their insides are cooled.

Then He, exalted, said: ﴿except boiling water and ghassaq﴾. This exception is disjunct (munqati') according to the grammarians (al-nahwiyyun), because the excepted item (al-mustathna) is not of the same kind as that from which it is excepted (al-mustathna minhu). The meaning is: they have nothing except this hamim (boiling water), which is water extremely hot in its heat, in addition to what we mentioned earlier, that they will be given water like molten metal (al-muhl) which scorches the faces [Al-Kahf 29], and they will be given to drink boiling water which cuts their intestines to pieces [Muhammad 15].

As for ﴿ghassaq﴾, the commentators said: ghassaq is a drink foul in smell and extremely cold, so there is gathered for them—we seek refuge in God—between water extremely hot and water extremely cold, so that they taste the punishment from both sides: from the side of heat and from the side of cold. Indeed, some of the people of tafsir said: what is meant by ghassaq is the pus of the people of the Fire and what flows from their bodies of stench, sweat, and other things.

In any case, the noble verse indicates that they will taste nothing but this drink which cuts their intestines by its heat and splits their livers by its cold; we ask God for well-being. When these kinds of punishment are combined, that is an increase in the intensity of the punishment upon them.

Then He, exalted, said: ﴿as a fitting recompense (jaza'an wifaqa)﴾ [An-Naba 26], meaning: they are recompensed with that, a recompense matching their deeds, without being wronged. God, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong the people at all, but it is the people who wrong themselves﴾ [Yunus 44]. So this recompense corresponds and matches their deeds.

Then He explained the correspondence, i.e., the correspondence of this punishment to the deeds, saying: ﴿Indeed, they did not expect a reckoning (27) and they denied Our signs with complete denial﴾ [An-Naba 27, 28]. So He mentioned their deviation in belief and their deviation in speech.

﴿Indeed, they did not expect a reckoning﴾ means: they did not hope to be called to account; rather they deny the reckoning and deny the resurrection, saying: ﴿It is not but our worldly life; we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time﴾ [Al-Jathiyah 24]. So they do not hope for a reckoning by which they would be held accountable, because they deny it. This is the belief of their hearts.

As for their tongues, they deny, saying: this is a lie, this is magic, this is madness, and similar things, as you read in the Book of God what these deniers say about the messengers of God. We stop at this point, and we ask God, exalted, to make it a blessed and beneficial meeting.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 78, verse 31–40:

We continue the commentary on Surah An-Naba where we stopped at the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, for the righteous there is an attainment (of success) (31), gardens and grapevines (32), and full-breasted [maidens] of equal age (33)﴾ [An-Naba 31–33], and onward to the end of what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, mentioned. These verses came after His saying: ﴿Indeed, Hell has been ever lying in wait (21) for the transgressors, a place of return﴾. That is because the Quran is mathani (oft-repeated, paired), in which matters are paired: when reward is mentioned in it, punishment is mentioned, and when punishment is mentioned, reward is mentioned; when the attributes of the believers are mentioned, the attributes of the disbelievers are mentioned, and so on. This is so that a person, when reading the Quran, is one who hopes and fears: when he reads what contains the reward of the believers, he yearns, hopes and aspires, and when he reads what contains the punishment of the disbelievers, he fears. Thus he travels towards Allah, the Exalted, between fear and hope, not feeling secure from the plan of Allah, nor despairing of the mercy of Allah.

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, said: A person should be between fear and hope in his worship of his Lord; whichever of the two prevails, its companion perishes.

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Indeed, for the righteous there is an attainment﴾. The righteous (al-muttaqun) are those who guard themselves against the punishment of Allah, by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions. Sometimes Allah commands taqwa of Himself, sometimes He commands taqwa of the Day of Reckoning, and sometimes He commands taqwa of the Fire. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And fear Allah that you may be successful (130) And fear the Fire﴾ [Al Imran 130–131], combining the command to fear Him with the command to fear the Fire. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned therein to Allah﴾ [Al-Baqarah 281], commanding taqwa of the Day of Reckoning.

All of this revolves around one meaning: that a person guard himself against the sacred prohibitions of his Lord, so he performs His obedience and refrains from His disobedience. The righteous are those who have carried out the commands of Allah and avoided the prohibitions of Allah. For these there is a mafaz (attainment), and mafaz is a place of success and also a time of success; so they are successful in their places and successful in their days.

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿gardens and grapevines﴾. This is a type of the mafaz. ﴿Gardens﴾ means great gardens, with many trees, varied trees.

﴿And grapevines﴾: 'a'nab is the plural of 'inab (grape), and it is part of the gardens, but He singled it out for mention.

﴿And full-breasted [maidens] (kawa'ib)﴾: kawa'ib is the plural of kā'ib, who is one whose breasts have become firm and have not sagged, but have risen and appeared like the knuckle-bone (ka'b); this is the most perfect that beauty of the bosom can be.

﴿Atraban﴾ means of one age, none of them differing from the others in age, as in the women of this world; for if they differed in age, the balance between them might be upset, and one of them might be grieved if she were not equal to the other. But they are of equal age.

﴿And a full cup﴾ [An-Naba 34]: that is, a cup filled to the brim. The intended meaning of the cup here is the cup of wine, though it may be of wine and other things, because in Paradise there are ﴿rivers of water unaltered, and rivers of milk whose taste never changes, and rivers of wine delicious to those who drink, and rivers of purified honey﴾ [Muhammad 15]. The cup "dihaq" means filled with wine, and it may be wine or other things.

﴿They will not hear therein any ill speech or lying﴾ [An-Naba 35]: they will not hear in Paradise any idle talk, that is, false speech with no good in it. ﴿Nor lying﴾ means no falsehood, so they do not lie, and none of them accuses another of lying, because they are on couches facing one another, and Allah has removed whatever resentment was in their breasts and made them brothers.

﴿A reward from your Lord, a gift accounted﴾ [An-Naba 36]: that is, they are recompensed with this, a reward from Allah, the Exalted, for their good deeds which they did in the world and by which they guarded against the prohibitions of Allah.

His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿hisaban﴾ means sufficient, derived from al-hasb, which is sufficiency; that is, this cup is a sufficient cup, such that they need nothing else with it, for the perfection of its pleasure and the completeness of its benefit.

Then He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Most Merciful﴾ [An-Naba 37]. Allah, the Exalted, is the Lord of everything. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, which He has made sacred, and to Him belongs everything﴾ [An-Naml 91]. He is the Lord of the seven layered heavens and the Lord of the earth, which is seven, as this is established in the Sunnah from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.

﴿And whatever is between them﴾ means the great created things between the heavens and the earth, such as clouds, vapours and orbits, and other things that we know of, and others that none knows but Allah, the Exalted.

His saying: ﴿They will not possess from Him any address (37). The Day the Spirit and the angels will stand in ranks﴾ [An-Naba 37–38] means that people do not possess speech from Allah, and no one can speak except by the permission of Allah. That is ﴿the Day the Spirit stands﴾, and it is Jibril; ﴿and the angels in ranks﴾ means in rows, row after row; because, as came in a hadith: "The angels of the lowest heaven descend and surround the creation, then the angels of the second heaven behind them, then the third, the fourth and the fifth." [[Ibn Abi Hatim recorded in his Tafsir (15089) with his chain from Ibn Abbas that he recited this verse: ﴿And the Day the sky will be split open by clouds and the angels will be sent down, descending﴾ [Al-Furqan 25], and Ibn Abbas said: Allah will gather the creation on the Day of Resurrection in one plain: the jinn, humankind, the beasts, the predators, the birds and all of creation. The lowest heaven will split and its people will descend, and they are more numerous than the jinn, humankind and all of creation, and they will surround the jinn, humankind and all creation. Then the second heaven will split and its people will descend, and they are more than the people of the lowest heaven and more than the jinn, humankind and all creation, and they will surround the angels who descended before them and the jinn, humankind and all creation. Then the third heaven will split and its people will descend... and so on for each heaven until the seventh heaven splits, and they are more than those who descended before them from the people of the heavens, and the jinn, humankind and all creation...]] and so on, in rows whose number none knows but He who created them, the Exalted.

﴿The Day the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks; none speak except one whom the Most Merciful has permitted, and he says what is correct﴾: that is, neither angels nor others speak, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And voices will be stilled before the Most Merciful, so you will hear nothing but a murmur﴾ [Taha 108].

﴿Except one whom the Most Merciful has permitted﴾ to speak, for he speaks only as he is permitted.

﴿And he says what is correct﴾: that is, he says a correct word that agrees with the good pleasure of Allah, the Exalted, and this is through intercession: when Allah permits someone to intercede, he intercedes for whom he is permitted, according to the extent of his permission.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿That is the true Day﴾ [An-Naba 39]: that is, that which We have informed you of is the true Day, and the truth is the opposite of falsehood, meaning the established reality in which truth prevails and justice prevails. ﴿The Day when neither wealth nor children will benefit, except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara 88–89]. May Allah help me and you in that Day.

﴿So whoever wills may take to his Lord a return﴾: that is, whoever wills, let him do a deed by which he returns to Allah and comes back to Allah, and that deed is righteous action agreeing with the good pleasure of Allah, the Exalted.

His saying: ﴿So whoever wills may take to his Lord a return﴾ is qualified by another verse, His saying: ﴿for whoever of you wills to take the straight path (28). And you do not will except that Allah wills, Lord of the worlds﴾ [At-Takwir 28–29]. That means we have the choice in what we pursue; no one compels us to anything. Yet our choice, our will and our desire return to Allah: ﴿And you do not will except that Allah wills﴾. Allah only made this clear in His Book so that a person does not rely on himself and on his own will, but knows that it is tied to the will of Allah, so that he turns to Allah in asking for guidance to what He loves and is pleased with. A person should not say, "I am free, I want as I wish and act as I wish." We say: the matter is so, but you are bound to the will of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment﴾ [An-Naba 40]: that is, We have made you fear a near punishment, which is the Day of Resurrection. The Day of Resurrection, in reality, O our brothers, is near, and even if the world remained for millions of years, it is near: ﴿As if, on the Day they see it, they had not remained but an evening or its morning﴾ [An-Nazi'at 46]. So this punishment with which Allah has warned us is near; between a person and it there is nothing but that he dies, and a person does not know when he will die. He may become morning and not reach evening, or reach evening and not reach morning. For this reason it is incumbent on us to be resolute in our deeds and to seize the opportunity before it is too late.

﴿The Day a man will look at what his hands have sent forth﴾: ﴿the man﴾ means every individual; he looks at what his hands have sent forth, and it is placed before him and his book is given to him, and it is said: ﴿Read your record; sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner﴾ [Al-Isra 14].

And the disbeliever, from the severity of the terror he sees and the punishment he witnesses, says: ﴿Oh, I wish I were dust!﴾ That is: I wish I had not been created, or I wish I had not been resurrected; or, when he sees the animals among whom Allah judges, and then He says to them, "Be dust," and they become dust, he wishes to be like the animals.

So His saying: ﴿I wish I were dust﴾ carries three meanings. The first meaning: "Would that I were dust and had not been created," because man was created from dust. The second meaning: "Would that I were dust and had not been resurrected," that is, that I were dust in the depths of graves. The third meaning: that when he sees the animals among whom Allah judged and said to them, "Be dust," and they became dust, he says: "Would that I were dust," meaning like these animals. And Allah knows best.

Here the Surah of An-Naba ends. In it are admonitions, wisdoms and signs of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, which are sufficient to produce certainty and faith. We ask Allah to benefit us and you by His Book, to make it an admonition to our hearts and a cure for what is in our breasts; indeed He is Generous and Bountiful. May the blessings and peace of Allah be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgement.

So this punishment with which Allah has warned us is near; between a person and it there is nothing but that he dies, and a person does not know when he will die. He may become morning and not reach evening, or reach evening and not reach morning. For this reason it is incumbent on us to be resolute in our deeds and to seize the opportunity before it is too late.

﴿The Day a man will look at what his hands have sent forth﴾: ﴿the man﴾ means every individual; he looks at what his hands have sent forth, and it is placed before him and his book is given to him, and it is said: ﴿Read your record; sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner﴾ [Al-Isra 14].

And the disbeliever, from the severity of the terror he sees and the punishment he witnesses, says: ﴿Oh, I wish I were dust!﴾ That is: I wish I had not been created, or I wish I had not been resurrected; or, when he sees the animals among whom Allah judges, and then He says to them, "Be dust," and they become dust, he wishes to be like the animals.

So His saying: ﴿I wish I were dust﴾ carries three meanings. The first meaning: "Would that I were dust and had not been created," because man was created from dust. The second meaning: "Would that I were dust and had not been resurrected," that is, that I were dust in the depths of graves. The third meaning: that when he sees the animals among whom Allah judged and said to them, "Be dust," and they became dust, he says: "Would that I were dust," meaning like these animals. And Allah knows best.

Here the Surah of An-Naba ends. In it are admonitions, wisdoms and signs of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, which are sufficient to produce certainty and faith. We ask Allah to benefit us and you by His Book, to make it an admonition to our hearts and a cure for what is in our breasts; indeed He is Generous and Bountiful. May the blessings and peace of Allah be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgement.
